answer: In a marketplace serving wharf operators, opal dealers and orchard growers, pay for verified jobs, never account creation. Each funded job has one signed claim ticket; a public spent-ticket set blocks reuse across identities. Hidden test cases check the delivered work before payment. Cap miner bonuses below the nonrefundable fee paid by the buyer. An attacker can invent buyers and workers, but each circular job loses money even after its bonus; splitting into a thousand accounts creates no extra tickets or reward budget.
